newsitem.title: UK: British Land issues jumbo convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: British Land issues jumbo convertible bond.

text.p: British Land Co Plc on Tuesday launched a 300 million stg convertible bond which its chairman John Ritblat said had met exceptional demand from its target audience of European investors.
"It is among the largest issues by a (British) property company and is going very well. The coupon is quite meaty...we wanted it to go well and bring in new investors," Ritblat told Reuters.

The 10-year bond issue will pay a coupon indicated at 6.25-6.50 percent. Paper was quoted at 99.875/100.125 on broker screens, straddling the par issue price. Fees totalled 2.5 points and SBC Warburg was the sole manager.

"When the market's there you take the opportunity. We are always refinancing in one way or another. There's big European demand for sterling and this will sell to European takers," Ritblat said, adding the current environment pre-EMU was a win-win situation for sterling bond issuers.

"If we (Britain) go into the single currency this will look an absolute bargain. We will have the same interest rates. They (rates) are bound to be lower and issues of this kind must be popular," he said.

"If we don't go in then, there may be people in Europe who will look at sterling once again as a very interesting place to be outside the fixed currency, perhaps their only alternative to the dollar."

The third stage of European economic and monetary union, including the introduction of the European Union's planned single currency, the euro, is prescribed by EU law to take place no later than January 1, 1999.
British Land's share price dipped after news of the convertible, with dealers citing fears about earnings being diluted.
Ritblat saw no dilution of earnings from the convertible bond issue.

"The coupon will be less than we would pay for fine-term banking where we might be paying, say, 30 (basis points) over LIBOR or 30 (b.p.) over gilts. Either way this (convertible) is going to come in under that and we will be a beneficiary.

Ritblat said the conversion premium on the convertible would add 10-12 pence stg to net assets per share. "It's a saving on our banking (costs), a valuable addition to the book and adds to net assets per share."
Ritblat said British Land's share price was lower today because "generally the property market is off after a very good rise (recently)".
By 1030 GMT British Land was 12.5p, or 2.14 percent, lower at 571p on volume of 2.1 million, while the FTSE-100 index was off 21.5 points (0.46 percent) at 4,623.7.
British Land joined the FTSE-100 index in March.
SBC Warburg has a greenshoe option to increase the size of the deal by 30 million stg (10 percent) to cover over-allotment.
Separately, IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said in a report published today that, from a bondholder perspective, the outlook was generally positive for British property companies.

"Hard evidence of an improvement within the sector is slowly appearing and this will affect property companies by varying degrees, depending on their exposure to the three core sectors: office, retail and industrial," IBCA said.
